motivation: The quantum Hall effect had always required strong external magnetic fields. In 2010 Fang, Dai and co-workers predicted that magnetically doped topological-insulator thin films could have a quantized Hall conductance at zero field, produced only by intrinsic magnetization and band topology. In 2013 Xue's team made this real. After four years of atomic-level control of molecular-beam-epitaxy growth of Cr-doped (Bi,Sb)2Te3 films, they observed a Hall resistance quantized at h/e^2 with no applied field. This was a true '0 to 1' result. It confirmed a topological state that Haldane had anticipated in 1988, and many groups have since reproduced it. It opened the field of dissipationless chiral edge transport, axion insulators and magnetic topological materials such as MnBi2Te4. It also points toward low-power electronics and topological quantum devices. It is an exemplary union of predictive theory and patient, precise materials experiment.
